traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Menyanthaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple or compound; veins pinnate or palmate; stipules absent; leaf rosettes basal; plants hermaphrodite; ovary superior or half inferior; floral cup absent; stems herbaceous; flowers solitary, in cymes, in heads or in panicles; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule or berry; parts of each whorl 5; stamens 5; carpels 2. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.division_pattern.note: Menyanthes has trifoliolate leaves with leaflets from one point (ternate), so palmate fits better than the order's pinnate; Nymphoides is simple. Our reading; APweb Asterales page (read 2026-10-16) does not describe the family.
